title: Canale and Gill the heroes as Paraguay hand Germany first World Cup shootout defeat
summary: Germany exited the World Cup in Boston not with a whimper or even a cry of pain, just an extended wrestle into the dust at the hands of a thrillingly dogged Paraguay, followed by the most extraordinary of penalty shootouts. Not only did Germany lose their first shootout since the original Panenka one of 1976. They did so in a whirl of errors, shanked kicks and what amounted to a sporting meltdown in the New England gloaming. Paraguay will now progress to play a last-16 tie in Philadelphia, but not before celebrating this result as surely the greatest in their football history. And rightly so, after a performance of wonderful heart and defensive discipline. Continue reading...

title: Untitled item
summary: #WC2026 #Football #DEUvPAR Interesting game, and a surprise ending, for some. To be honest, when the penalties started, I said to my friends that I though the Paraguayans would win it, as I didn't have as much confidence in Neuer's ability to have a good enough leap after 120 hot minutes of football as I did the other fellow. And it turned out I had read it well. Neuer only saved one, and it was a poorly taken pen (as, to be fair, were the two saved by PAR). But I expect better from Die Mannschaft, and I don't think I'm alone. Will be very surprised if Nagelsmann sticks around after that. He made some very odd decisions - like bringing Neuer out of retirement to have a last hurrah, while leaving an excellent young prospect like Atubolu at home. For my money, the early exit is down to Nagelsmann. As to the disputed goal, that would have been Germany's second...I'm afraid this old ref is going to disappoint, my German friends, as I feel the VAR was correct. The push on the keeper was enough, given his half-turned and off-balance position, to push him over. No way a keeper in a knockout game like that is going to fall over easily and hope for a call. So I would have to have reluctantly but I think correctly called it back. The principle for me would be, the player pushing shouldn't have his hands up on the other player at all. There's no legitimate play he can make by doing that, only fouls, so that initial choice is already gonna have me watching him. And when he pushes the man down...I have to call that. For me, the "miracle" set piece increases we've had are not the least bit mystifying: they correspond with the end of enforcement of the Laws while awaiting a corner kick. Both sides push and shove, using both arms, wrapping up other players, boxing in the keeper...this is all foul play. I don't want such play to be rewarded with goals. If it is, then we will soon have a 3-2 UCL Final...with five corner kicks scored, all by bullying the defenders. Me? Nah.
